originality.rationale: A published 2026-11-08 SCOPE paper already gives the exact finite 2-by-2 Fourier block spectrum of the SAME uniform wheel spanning-tree indicator covariance for every rim size, including the Green kernel and all pair inclusion probabilities. The assigned coordinate Walsh Gram matrix is exactly G=4C+(1-2p)(1-2p)^T. On wheels p_e is already explicitly K_ee in that earlier proof, so its two constant mean blocks and all nonconstant Gram Fourier blocks are directly determined. The new n^3 condition asymptotic follows from that paper’s lambda_min(C)~pi^2/(sqrt5*n^2), mean spoke-minus-rim vector of norm squared 2n(1-2/sqrt5)^2, and the rank-one update; all-n closed forms simplify earlier finite Fourier-block entries. Thus the single final claim is already mathematically covered as an elementary consequence of the stronger earlier complete wheel-covariance description even though the word Walsh and the cubic coefficient do not appear there. Mere vocabulary/normalization change cannot establish O.
residual_risks: All-n algebraic extrema require checking degeneracies, but no independent new unentailed invariant remains after the earlier full finite matrix description; no claim of exact word-for-word duplication.

value.rationale: Sampling Walsh characters of a natural tree orbit is mathematically motivated, and the proof is correct. However the exact Gram operator is just four times the earlier completely evaluated same-object covariance plus its explicit rank-one mean term. The principal n^3 growth comes mechanically from the prior n^-2 centered gap and the elementary O(n) mean contribution. This re-expression is not a substantive new mathematical gap independent of the already available finite covariance spectrum.
residual_risks: Prior result treats vertex-uniform spanning-tree edge incidence at every n>=3, with complete finite H_j blocks; differences of centering yield no new distribution or parameter.

limitations: Scientific rejection is due to prior implication and lack of independent value, not a numerical/test failure; entire package preserved for server relocation.
